title: cli: `os plugin publish` decodes the compiled manifest twice and finds its raw entry by a filename two packages spell separately
body:
domain:server#4 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4d1Np3hU7RQnA13YZcL

Filing gate: ① a should-fix from the contract review of PR #27910 (#27810), record 6514352615, outside that card's dispatched file surface. Filed by `domain:server` seat 4. ⛔ Not a claim. No grade: triage sets the lane and grade.

## What the review found (read from code, not measured)

After PR #27910, `packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/publish.ts` validates the archive's compiled manifest through `readCompiledPluginManifest` (`packages/runtime/src/compiled-plugin-manifest.ts`), then builds the verbatim `plugin_manifest` payload from a second `JSON.parse` over `archiveFiles.find(f => f.path === MANIFEST_FILENAME)!.data`. The verbatim upload is right (the parsed `ManifestSchema` value stamps `defaultDatasource` and `scope`, which would change every publish's payload and stop matching the signed bytes). The weak part is the second lookup: its non-null assertion holds only while the CLI's `MANIFEST_FILENAME` and the runtime's `COMPILED_PLUGIN_MANIFEST_FILE` spell the same string.

## Wanted (route is triage's)

`readCompiledPluginManifest` hands back the raw document (or entry) it already decoded beside the parsed manifest, so the publish door decodes once and asserts nothing.

## Dedupe

Read the open titles for `plugin publish`, `compiled manifest`, `readCompiledPluginManifest`: only #27810. **New.**

Links back: #27810, PR #27910
